**CEO Commentary and Highlights**


Rodger Levenson, Chairman, CEO and President, said, "WSFS continued to perform well in the third quarter with a 25% year-over-year increase in core EPS(2). Our results include an expanded net interest margin, solid loan growth, and continued strong momentum in our Wealth and Trust franchise, which generated year-over-year fee growth of 30%. Additionally, we continued to execute our capital return framework through dividends and share repurchases, repurchasing nearly six percent of outstanding shares(3) in the first three quarters of 2026. We look forward to finishing the year out strong in the fourth quarter, while providing momentum as we enter 2027."


Overall highlights include:


- Core EPS of $1.75, an increase of 5% compared to 2Q 2026 and 25% compared to 3Q 2025.
- Core ROA (2) of 1.58%, an increase of 3bps compared to 2Q 2026 and 10bps compared to 3Q 2025.
- Gross loans and leases grew 5% annualized quarter-over-quarter.
- Net interest margin (NIM) of 3.88%, an increase of 1bp compared to 2Q 2026.
- Wealth and Trust delivered 30% year-over-year fee growth, continuing to produce consistent double-digit growth.


- WSFS Institutional Services ® fees increased 45%, The Bryn Mawr Trust Company of Delaware (BMT of DE), our personal trust business, increased 22%, and Private Wealth Management increased 14%.


- Our core efficiency ratio (2) was 56.1%, an improvement of 223bps compared to 2Q 2026 and 345bps compared to 3Q 2025.
- Repurchased $59.6 million of common stock (1.5% of outstanding shares (4)) and paid quarterly dividends of $10.2 million for a total capital return of $69.8 million.


(2)As used in this press release, core EPS, core ROA, and core efficiency ratio are non-GAAP financial measures. These non-GAAP financial measures exclude certain pre-tax adjustments and the tax impact of such adjustments. For a reconciliation of non-GAAP financial measures to their most directly comparable GAAP measures, see "Non-GAAP Reconciliation" at the end of the press release.


(3)Year-to-date 2026 repurchases represent 5.6% of outstanding shares as of December 31, 2025.


(4)3Q 2026 repurchases represent 1.5% of outstanding shares as of June 30, 2026.

At September 30, 2026, WSFS’ gross loan and lease portfolio increased $162.6 million, or 1% (not annualized), when compared with June 30, 2026. Home Lending continued to generate strong performance across both mortgages and home equity, with overall growth of 6%. Commercial loans increased 1%, led by growth in C&I, as well as an increase in commercial small business leases. This growth was partially offset by continued runoff of the Spring EQ portfolio.


Gross loans and leases at September 30, 2026 increased 5% when compared with September 30, 2025. Excluding the impacts from the sale of the credit card portfolio and runoff of Spring EQ, gross loans and leases increased 7%. This growth was driven by increases in residential mortgage (27%), home equity (20%), and C&I (9%), partially offset by a decline in commercial small business leases.

Total client deposits decreased $619.5 million, or 3% (not annualized), when compared with June 30, 2026. The reduction in ending deposits reflects the expected outflow of transactional deposits at the end of the prior quarter within WSFS Institutional Services® and Commercial. These declines were partially offset by growth within interest-bearing demand (7%) due to seasonal increases in municipal deposits, money market (2%), and time deposits (2%). Average deposits increased slightly during the quarter, led by Commercial and Small Business.


Total client deposits increased $1.2 billion, or 7% from September 30, 2025, with core deposits increasing 9%. This growth was driven by a 16% increase in noninterest demand deposits, with growth in WSFS Institutional Services®, Commercial, and Consumer. Money market grew 9%, driven by growth across all business lines, while time deposits decreased 9%. Noninterest demand deposits increased to 33% of total client deposits, compared to 31% last year.


The deposit base remains well-diversified, with 56% of quarterly average client deposits coming from outside of our Consumer business. No- and low-cost deposit accounts(6) represented 58% of average total client deposits with a weighted average cost of 31bps for the quarter. The loan-to-deposit ratio(7) was 73% at September 30, 2026, providing capacity to fund ongoing loan growth.


(6) Includes noninterest demand, interest-bearing demand, and savings deposit accounts.

Net interest income increased $4.1 million, or 2% (not annualized), compared to 2Q 2026, primarily driven by higher average loan balances and higher yields on loans and investment securities. The higher yields were partially offset by higher deposit costs as we continued to see elevated deposit pricing competition.


Net interest income increased $12.6 million, or 7%, compared to 3Q 2025, primarily driven by lower deposit costs and higher average loan balances. These increases were partially offset by lower loan yields following Federal Funds Rate cuts in 2025.


Total loan yields were 6.26%, an increase of 2bps when compared to 2Q 2026 and a decrease of 38bps when compared to 3Q 2025. The year-over-year decrease was primarily driven by the impact of the aforementioned interest rate cuts.


Total client deposit costs were 1.33% and interest-bearing deposit costs were 2.05%, increases of 4bps and 5bps, respectively, compared to 2Q 2026. Total client deposit costs decreased 29bps and interest-bearing deposit costs decreased 32bps compared to 3Q 2025. The quarter-over-quarter increase in total client deposit costs reflects elevated deposit cost competition and mix shift. The year-over-year decrease was driven primarily by deposit repricing actions and mix shift.


Net interest margin of 3.88% increased 1bp compared to 2Q 2026, primarily due to higher average loan balances and higher investment yields, partially offset by higher deposit costs. Net interest margin decreased 3bps from 3Q 2025 primarily due to the impact of the 2025 interest rate cuts, partially offset by higher investment yields and favorable balance sheet mix.

Overall, most asset quality metrics were stable with delinquencies reaching their lowest level in two years, while year-to-date net charge-offs were 3bps of average gross loans.


Problem assets increased $57.5 million compared to June 30, 2026, driven by several downgrades, primarily within multifamily and construction, partially offset by payoffs. Delinquencies decreased $2.9 million, or 3bps of gross loans, compared to June 30, 2026, driven by commercial payoffs. Problem assets decreased 16% and delinquencies decreased 11% compared to September 30, 2025.


Nonperforming assets (NPAs) increased $1.7 million, or 1bp of total assets, compared to June 30, 2026. The increase in NPAs was primarily driven by a student housing-related loan, partially offset by payoffs of a C&I loan and a CRE office loan.


Net recoveries on loans and leases for the quarter were $0.6 million compared to net charge-offs of $7.1 million in 2Q 2026. The quarter included recoveries of $7.6 million from the payoff of NPAs noted above.


Total net credit costs increased $4.4 million when compared to 2Q 2026, driven by a specific reserve of $8.1 million on the student housing-related loan mentioned above and a $2.0 million write-down of an OREO property, partially offset by the aforementioned recoveries.


The ACL on loans and leases was $185.2 million as of September 30, 2026, an increase of $8.0 million when compared to June 30, 2026, and the ACL coverage increased 4bps to 1.36%.


(8)Problem assets includes all criticized, classified, and nonperforming loans as well as other real estate owned (OREO).


**Core Fee Revenue(9)**


Core fee revenue (noninterest income) of $91.0 million decreased $1.2 million, or 1%, compared to 2Q 2026. We continued to see strong momentum in Wealth and Trust, which had an increase of $2.5 million, or 5%, due to growth across WSFS Institutional Services® and Private Wealth Management. This increase was more than offset by a decline in Capital Markets revenue from lower demand for interest rate swaps due to the rate environment, as well as lower Cash Connect® revenue driven by a decrease in cash volume.


Core fee revenue increased $3.0 million, or 3%, compared to 3Q 2025. The increase was driven by a $12.5 million, or 30%, increase in Wealth and Trust, including 45% growth in WSFS Institutional Services®, driven by both Corporate Trust and Global Capital Markets, 22% growth in BMT of DE, and 14% growth in Private Wealth Management. These increases were partially offset by a $3.6 million decrease in Cash Connect®, primarily due to the impact of interest rate cuts in 2025 and lower ATM volumes, as well as lower gains on the sale of mortgage and SBA loans as we retained more of our originated loans.


For 3Q 2026, our core fee revenue ratio(9) was 31.6% compared to 32.3% in both 2Q 2026 and 3Q 2025. Fee revenue diversification is a strategic priority and we continue to see momentum in our fee businesses, particularly in Wealth and Trust.


(9)As used in this press release, core fee revenue and core fee revenue ratio are non-GAAP financial measures. These non-GAAP financial measures exclude certain pre-tax adjustments and the tax impact of such adjustments. For a reconciliation of these and other non-GAAP financial measures to their most directly comparable GAAP measures, see "Non-GAAP Reconciliation" at the end of the press release.


**Core Noninterest Expense(10)**


Core noninterest expense of $161.5 million decreased $4.8 million, or 3% (not annualized), compared to 2Q 2026. The decrease is primarily due to lower external fraud losses, including recoveries of previously incurred losses, lower medical costs, and lower professional fees which were primarily driven by a recovery of legal expenses. These decreases were partially offset by an increase in occupancy expenses and loan workout and other credit costs due to the write-down of an existing OREO property.


Core noninterest expense decreased $0.7 million, or less than 1%, compared to 3Q 2025. Excluding Cash Connect® external funding costs, which decreased due to lower rates and ATM volume, core noninterest expense increased $2.6 million(10), or 2%. This increase reflects higher salaries and benefits primarily due to merit increases, higher equipment expenses from client transaction costs in Wealth and Trust and continued investment in technology across the franchise, as well as the OREO write-down noted above. These increases were partially offset by lower external fraud losses and professional fees.


Our core efficiency ratio(10) was 56.1% in 3Q 2026, compared to 58.3% in 2Q 2026 and 59.5% in 3Q 2025, reflecting our focus on expense discipline while continuing to invest in the franchise.


**Income Taxes**


We recorded a $28.3 million income tax provision in 3Q 2026, compared to $26.8 million in 2Q 2026 and $24.4 million in 3Q 2025. The increases in income tax provision compared to 2Q 2026 and 3Q 2025 were primarily due to higher income before taxes.


The effective tax rate was 24.1% in 3Q 2026 compared to 24.1% in 2Q 2026 and 24.2% in 3Q 2025. The decrease in effective tax rate compared to 3Q 2025 is primarily due to increased federal tax credits.


(10)As used in this press release, core noninterest expense, adjusted core noninterest expense, and core efficiency ratio are non-GAAP financial measures. These non-GAAP financial measures exclude certain pre-tax adjustments and the tax impact of such adjustments. For a reconciliation of these and other non-GAAP financial measures to their most directly comparable GAAP measures, see "Non-GAAP Reconciliation" at the end of the press release.


**Capital Management**


Capital ratios remain strong and are all substantially in excess of the “well-capitalized” regulatory benchmarks at September 30, 2026, with a Common Equity Tier 1 capital ratio and Tier 1 capital ratio of 13.74%, Tier 1 leverage ratio of 10.40%, and Total Risk-based capital ratio of 15.47%.


WSFS’ total stockholders’ equity decreased $108.8 million, or 4%, during 3Q 2026. The decrease was primarily due to an increase in accumulated other comprehensive loss of $131.2 million, driven by market-value decreases on available-for-sale investment securities, and capital returns to stockholders of $69.8 million, partially offset by quarterly earnings of $89.3 million.


WSFS’ tangible common equity(11) decreased $104.4 million, or 6%, compared to June 30, 2026, primarily due to the reasons noted above. WSFS’ common equity to assets ratio decreased 19bps to 11.82% and tangible common equity to tangible assets ratio(12) decreased 29bps to 7.82% at September 30, 2026.


At September 30, 2026, book value per share was $51.58, a decrease of $1.39, or 3% (not annualized), from June 30, 2026, and tangible book value per share(11) was $32.67, a decrease of $1.57, or 5% (not annualized), from June 30, 2026, primarily due to the increase in accumulated other comprehensive loss. Book value per share increased $1.91, or 4%, and tangible book value per share increased $0.56, or 2%, compared to 3Q 2025.


During 3Q 2026, WSFS repurchased 748,970 shares of common stock for an aggregate of $59.6 million and paid quarterly cash dividends of $10.2 million. Total capital returns to stockholders through share repurchases and quarterly dividends was $69.8 million. WSFS has 8,451,059 shares, or approximately 17% of outstanding shares as of September 30, 2026, available for repurchase.


The Board of Directors approved a quarterly cash dividend of $0.20 per share of common stock. The dividend will be paid on November 20, 2026 to stockholders of record as of November 6, 2026.

Wealth and Trust pre-tax income was $52.7 million, which increased $5.0 million, or 10% (not annualized), compared to 2Q 2026, driven by increases in net interest income of $3.0 million and fee revenue of $2.3 million.


The increase in net interest income was driven by higher yields on interest-earning assets. The increase in fee revenue was driven by higher deal activity in WSFS Institutional Services® and higher AUM-based fees.


Wealth and Trust pre-tax income increased $18.3 million, or 53%, compared to 3Q 2025, driven by increases in fee revenue of $12.4 million and net interest income of $10.6 million. These increases were partially offset by an increase in noninterest expense of $3.0 million.


The increase in fee revenue was driven by growth in WSFS Institutional Services®, Private Wealth Management, and BMT of DE. The increase in net interest income was due to higher noninterest deposit balances in WSFS Institutional Services®. The increase in noninterest expense was primarily due to higher salaries and benefits and client transaction costs, partially offset by a recovery of legal fees.

**About WSFS Financial Corporation**


WSFS Financial Corporation is a multibillion-dollar financial services company. Its primary subsidiary, WSFS Bank, is the oldest and largest locally headquartered bank and wealth management franchise in the Greater Philadelphia and Delaware region. As of September 30, 2026, WSFS Financial Corporation had $22.1 billion in assets on its balance sheet and $109.5 billion in assets under management and administration. WSFS operates from 115 offices, 87 of which are banking offices, located in Pennsylvania (59), Delaware (38), New Jersey (14), Florida (2), Nevada (1) and Virginia (1) and provides comprehensive financial services including commercial banking, consumer banking, treasury management, and trust and wealth management. Other subsidiaries or divisions include Arrow Land Transfer, Bryn Mawr Trust Advisors, LLC, Bryn Mawr Trust®, The Bryn Mawr Trust Company of Delaware, Cash Connect®, NewLane Finance®, WSFS Wealth® Management, LLC, WSFS Institutional Services®, and WSFS Mortgage®. Serving the Greater Delaware Valley since 1832, WSFS Bank is one of the ten oldest banks in the United States continuously operating under the same name. For more information, please visit[www.wsfsbank.com](https://cts.businesswire.com/ct/CT?id=smartlink&url=http%3A%2F%2Fwww.wsfsbank.com&esheet=54625867&newsitemid=20261022626993&lan=en-US&anchor=www.wsfsbank.com&index=2&md5=bafcf2bb210aceda595efe2c92dac77f) .
